title: Unusual Active Directory replication traffic between domain controllers
description: High volume of replication traffic between DC01 and DC02 outside the usual schedule, flagged as possible domain replication abuse.
justification: Both hosts are domain controllers of the same domain; replication is their normal function, and the volume matched a schema update window confirmed by the client. A tuning request was filed for this DC pair.
note: Note: Replication traffic between the two domain controllers DC01 and DC02. The client confirmed a schema update at that time. Benign, closing.
team_notes: Teams, shift handover: Third spike this month, always during the schema update window. Tuning filed for the DC pair.

title: Successful sign-in from an unusual country
description: User signed in successfully from Germany, a country never seen for this account. MFA was completed.
justification: The user confirmed business travel to Germany. MFA passed and no other anomaly was found on the account.
note: Note: Sign-in from Germany confirmed by the user as business travel, MFA completed. Nothing malicious, closing.
team_notes: Email from the client: 'Our Munich office visit was planned, sorry for the late notice.' Travel confirmed after the fact.

title: Successful sign-in from an unusual country
description: User signed in successfully from a country never seen for this account, followed by the creation of a mailbox rule. No travel notice on file.
justification: No travel confirmation, and an inbox rule was created right after the sign-in. Escalated for investigation, password reset, and session revocation.
note: Note: Escalated. Unconfirmed sign-in from a new country followed by mailbox rule creation. Client asked to reset the password and revoke sessions.
team_notes: Teams, on-call chat: No travel notice anywhere. The inbox rule is the red flag, escalate and get the password reset fast.

title: Possible DNS tunneling from workstation
description: Long DNS queries to an unusual domain at regular intervals.
justification: The queries were traced to the telemetry endpoint of the endpoint security agent; the domain belongs to the vendor. A tuning request was filed.
note: Note: DNS traffic traced to the security agent telemetry endpoint, vendor domain. Benign, closing.
team_notes: Teams: Vendor confirmed the telemetry domain is theirs. Added to the tuning list.

title: Malicious hash match on guest network device
description: A file hash matching a known malware signature was seen on a device connected to the guest Wi-Fi.
justification: The client confirmed the device sits on the isolated guest network with no access to internal resources; the file was a test sample from their own security training.
note: Note: Hash match on the isolated guest network, test sample confirmed by the client. No exposure, closing.
team_notes: Email from the client: 'That device is our training laptop on the guest Wi-Fi, the sample is from our own course.'

title: Password spray against VPN portal
description: Many failed sign-ins across several accounts from one external IP, no successful logon.
justification: All attempts failed; MFA and lockout policies held. The source IP was blocked on the client firewall.
note: Note: Password spray with no successful logon, source blocked. Nothing out of the ordinary, closing.
team_notes: Shift handover: Spray hit the VPN again overnight, zero successes. IP blocked at the firewall.

title: Periodic outbound beaconing from workstation
description: Regular small outbound connections every 30 minutes to the same external domain.
justification: The traffic is the update mechanism of the marketing team's approved analytics software.
note: Note: Beaconing identified as the update traffic of an approved application. Benign, closing.
team_notes: Teams: Marketing confirmed the analytics tool is approved and paid for. The beacon is its update check.

title: New administrator account created
description: A new account with administrative rights was created outside business hours.
justification: The client confirmed a planned maintenance window; the account was created by their IT provider for a migration and removed afterwards.
note: Note: Admin account creation confirmed by the client as planned maintenance. Closing.
team_notes: Email from the client: 'Maintenance window approved, the new admin account is our provider, it will be removed Friday.'

title: Internal network scan detected
description: Port scan across the internal range from a single host.
justification: The host is the client's vulnerability scanner; the scan matched the scheduled weekly assessment.
note: Note: Scan traced to the scheduled vulnerability scanner. Expected activity, closing.
team_notes: Teams: The scanner runs every Tuesday night. If it fires outside that window, look again.

title: Token theft indicators on user workstation
description: Impossible travel plus token replay artifacts in the sign-in logs.
justification: Signs of session token reuse from a second location. Escalated; the client disabled the account and revoked sessions.
note: Note: Escalated. Token replay indicators found. Client asked to keep the account disabled pending investigation.
team_notes: Teams, on-call chat: Token replay is real until proven otherwise. The account stayed disabled all weekend.

title: Sudo privilege escalation on Linux server
description: A user ran sudo to root repeatedly during the evening.
justification: The activity matched the monthly patching window; the commands were package updates only. A tuning request was filed for this host and account during patch windows.
note: Note: Sudo activity during the patching window, update commands only. Benign, closing.
team_notes: Shift handover: Patching night on the Linux boxes, sudo noise is expected until 23:00.

title: User reported phishing email, link clicked
description: A user reported a phishing email after clicking the link and entering credentials on a fake page.
justification: Credentials were entered on the fake page. Escalated so the client can reset the password, revoke sessions, and check for mailbox rules.
note: Note: Escalated. Credentials entered on a phishing page. Client asked to reset the password and review mailbox rules.
team_notes: Email from the user: 'I clicked and typed my password before I realized.' A fast escalation saved the account.

title: Log source silent for 24 hours
description: No logs received from a firewall forwarder for 24 hours.
justification: The forwarder service had stopped; the client restarted it and the logs resumed. The gap is explained.
note: Note: Log gap caused by a stopped forwarder service, restarted by the client, logs flowing again. Closing.
team_notes: Teams: The forwarder service dies about once a quarter. A restart brings the logs back, the gap is explainable.

title: RDP brute force from internal host
description: Repeated failed RDP logons from the internal jump host toward several servers.
justification: A misconfigured service account on the jump host was retrying with an old password; the client corrected the configuration and the failures stopped.
note: Note: Failed RDP logons traced to a misconfigured service account, corrected by the client. Closing.
team_notes: Shift handover: The service account password was changed on Friday, the jump host kept retrying the old one.
